correctness.rationale: On a finite chain, forward confluence forces empty rows to precede nonempty rows and forces maxima of successive nonempty fibers to be weakly increasing; conversely these two conditions are sufficient because any required refinement can be chosen at the later row maximum. For fixed weakly increasing maxima \(m_1\le\cdots\le m_k\), each nonempty row has \(2^{m_i-1}\) possible fibers, so summing gives the complete homogeneous polynomial \(h_k(1,2,\ldots,2^{n-1})={n+k-1\brack k}_2\). A fresh direct enumeration of every binary relation for \(n=1,2,3,4\) reproduced totals \(2,11,198,13377\) and agreed exactly with the Gaussian-binomial formula. The asymptotic is obtained by normalizing the \(k=n-j\) summands; fixed \(j>0\) is exponentially suppressed, while the top summand has the standard Gaussian-binomial product limit.

A separate 2026 FIK-complexity paper was a plausible same-logic source, but an authorized full-text retrieval request was safety-blocked; it was not retried or bypassed. Its accessible material concerns proof-system complexity, so the unread remainder is recorded as a residual risk rather than treated as a failure.
